reason: Burgess 1991 records only cryptospores before the late Aeronian, with trilete Ambitisporites from the late Aeronian; the taxon A. vavrdovae (= Imperfectotriletes vavrdovae) is a hilate cryptospore, so a Hirnantian-early Aeronian trilete record is unsupported.

Late Ordovician trilete spores are plausible, but Emphanisporites protophanus is a Silurian-Devonian form and the source is an acritarch paper; later Ghelli Fm work finds only 2 trilete species among mostly cryptospores.
Extant moss species (Polytrichum alpestre, Funaria hygrometrica) in the Ordovician are contamination or misidentification (Timofeev 1976).
Laevigatosporites desmoinesensis is a Pennsylvanian monolete spore, so its presence in the Red Mountain Fm is contamination or a mis-dated record.

Dulhuntyispora is a Permian genus and Acanthotriletes is implausible in the Silurian; the whole-Silurian age is a pooled label from a palynoplankton paper (da Costa 1982) and the spores are probably younger or misidentified.
Gray 1985 Vila Maria Fm (Parana Basin) Tetrahedraletes medinensis is a standard Llandovery cryptospore, and the Llandovery Brazil record appears in the Wellman et al. 2013 compilation.
Schizaeoisporites is a Mesozoic-Cenozoic genus; an informal sp.I in the Katian-Telychian is a misidentification or contaminant, and the Katian-Telychian span is a pooled Deerlijk label.

Lycospora, Calamospora and Apiculatisporis are Devonian-Carboniferous genera; a whole-Silurian age in a regional review (Shah 1979) is an erroneous or pooled age and the identifications are anachronistic.

Ambitisporites imperfectus is a Richardson Libyan taxon with an Early Aeronian type record; its extension back to the Katian rests on a pooled Katian-Telychian label for the whole paper and is not independently corroborated.
A. vavrdovae (new, Richardson) is now Imperfectotriletes vavrdovae, a hilate cryptospore, so the taxon is credibly present in Llandovery Libya but not as a true trilete spore.

Cryptospores are accepted from the Dapingian (Rubinstein et al. 2010); a Floian Tetrahedraletes sp. from an integrative review (Vergel 2002) is uncorroborated and probably a dating imprecision or non-cryptospore.
Middle Arenigian hilate monads (Laevolancis, Imperfectotriletes sp.) predate the accepted Dapingian onset; they may be Dapingian-equivalent but are uncorroborated and of open nomenclature.

Ambitisporites avitus is credible in Llandovery-Wenlock marine Silurian of NW Argentina (Rubinstein & Brussa 1999 report Telychian and Homerian trilete spores); the stage span is broad and the source is pre-1980.

Punctatisporites dilutus (= Ambitisporites dilutus) is credible somewhere in the Silurian, but the source is a 1973 review with a whole-Silurian label and Lophotriletes sp. is a questionable Silurian record.
Archaeozonotriletes siluriensis from a 1974 borehole report is labelled only as Silurian, so the age is pooled and the Soviet-era identification is unverified.
Tetrahedraletes medinensis is a long-ranging, common early Silurian cryptospore, and the Kuh-e-Boghou record (Ghavidel-Syooki 2003) is a modern palynostratigraphic study.

Archaeozonotriletes chulus nanus is a well-known late Llandovery-Wenlock (Telychian-Homerian) form in the Wenlock type area (Bassett 1989 volume); the Aeronian lower bound looks like a mapping artefact but the taxon sits inside the window.

A 1971 Leiotriletes sp. from the Early Llandovery of Deerlijk is an open-nomenclature smooth trilete that may be a misidentified cryptospore; Wellman et al. 2013 list only Moyeria for the Llandovery of Belgium.

Ambitisporites avitus was described from the Lower Silurian of Libya (Hoffmeister 1959) and is listed for Llandovery Libya by Wellman et al. 2013; the Rhuddanian-Pridoli label comes from an in situ catalogue (Balme 1995) and is pooled.

Gotland has no Rhuddanian-Aeronian strata and the source is an acritarch monograph; Brochotriletes sp. (a reticulate trilete) is unlikely in the Llandovery, and Ambitisporites sp. is plausible only from the Telychian.
Laevigatosporites is a Carboniferous-Permian monolete genus, and the whole-Silurian age from a regional review is erroneous or pooled.
Wellman 2000 describes the Silurian Hawiyah-151 core with abundant cryptospores, consistent with the Saudi Arabian Silurian assemblages of Steemans et al. 2000.
Ambitisporites sp. is expected in the Llandovery Tuscarora Fm (Gensel et al. 1990; Johnson 1985 give a Llandovery age) and trilete Ambitisporites is accepted by the Telychian.

Wellman et al. 2013 list Ambitisporites dilutus and A. avitus for Aeronian Libya, matching the Burgess 1991 first late Aeronian occurrence; A. vavrdovae is a hilate cryptospore, but A. dilutus carries the trilete claim.
Tetrahedraletes, Nodospora and Dyadospora are typical Rhuddanian cryptospores from Libya (Hill et al. 1985), matching the Wellman et al. 2013 Rhuddanian Libya assemblage.
Burgess 1991 records a diverse older cryptospore assemblage from the latest Ordovician to late Aeronian, including Rhuddanian Velatitetras, Rimosotetras and Dyadospora.

Ambitisporites dilutus is documented from the late Aeronian of the Llandovery area (Burgess 1991; Richardson 1989 global-standard volume); the Rhuddanian part of the window is unsupported but the taxon sits within it.
